races.name: By Chen Presidential Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Clementines Star
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form at 5-6f but stepping up to 7f is an open stamina question; gets the uncontested lead here which flatters her chance, though her natural style is prominent rather than a pure front-runner and the extra furlong may find her out late.|

runners_data.name: Dolo's Star
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa booking is a notable upgrade in jockey quality; showed a 2nd at 5f on standard going but has been tried over 6f at Goodwood and the step to 7f is unproven, sitting in behind from her hold-up position and needing a clear run late.|

runners_data.name: Princess Honey Bee
runners_data.note: Returns from a 325-day absence which is a significant fitness query; has placed twice at 7f and further, making her the most proven stayer in the field on paper, but the layoff means fitness rather than ability is the key risk.|

races.paceDynamic: Clementines Star is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner maiden and will lead from the outset at a tempo she controls entirely, with no rival capable or inclined to challenge her for the front. Dolo's Star and Princess Honey Bee are both hold-up types who will settle in behind, meaning Clementines Star dictates every yard of the 7f trip at Thirsk on her own terms. The critical question is whether she can convert her uncontested lead into victory at the finish, or whether one of the two closers can reel her in over the final furlong on good ground. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent or front-running profile — Clementines Star gets a dream lead, and any hold-up horse must produce a sustained finish to peg her back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Clementines Star sets a sustainable, measured gallop and the hold-up pair fail to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Clementines Star controls every fraction unchallenged, getting cover from wind and dictating her own rhythm; with only two rivals to pass her and both needing a strong late surge, the lead is hers to lose over 7f at Thirsk.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Clementines Star either goes too fast early or ties up in the final 100 yards, allowing the hold-up pair to mow her down.
scenarios.body: Dolo's Star or Princess Honey Bee, tracking a fading leader, can produce a sharp late challenge if the pace proves slightly too hot; Silvestre De Sousa's experience on Dolo's Star gives that horse an edge in timing a run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Dead Heat
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so moderate that all three converge at the finish and the race comes down to a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A crawl turns this into a sprint, which marginally helps the hold-up horses if they have more raw speed, but the small field limits tactical variation significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Clementines Star Fades Badly
scenarios.trigger: If Clementines Star proves unable to see out 7f on good ground after dominating shorter trips.
scenarios.body: With most of her history over 5-6f, stamina doubt at 7f is a genuine concern; if she weakens sharply from the 2f pole, Princess Honey Bee — with two runs already at 7f+ — is best placed to inherit.

watchPoints.text: Princess Honey Bee's 325-day absence is the single biggest flag in the race — if she returns fit, her 7f+ form profile makes her dangerous, but fitness off such a long layoff is unverifiable.
Clementines Star's stamina at 7f is untested — all meaningful form is at 5-6f, and if she ties up approaching the final furlong, the race opens up immediately for the closers.
Dolo's Star's form at 11/6f Goodwood last time is a low point to carry forward, and while the jockey upgrade is real, her overall form figures (5420) do not inspire confidence at this distance.
With only three runners and two hold-up horses, any wide draw or traffic issue is almost irrelevant — the race reduces to whether Clementines Star's lead is catchable over the final 2f at Thirsk.
Good going suits all three on available evidence, so no runner gains a material surface edge — the race shape and stamina are the dominant factors to assess.

races.name: Best Ticket Deals Online @Thirskraces Book Now Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Britain
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with two wins over this mile on good ground; her hold-up style is well-suited to this shape if Sandy Craic burns off the prominent types, and jockey Kyle McHugh's 7lb claim is a meaningful weight relief on a horse returning after a 308-day absence.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Britain won twice in her last five starts and already has form over today's distance, though her latest run was well below that level. The main worry is fitness, with a near-year gap since that outing.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Recent Haydock second and a low-pressure lead to himself here is a significant tactical gift; the David O'Meara yard is 2/49 in the 14-day window which tempers enthusiasm, but the race-shape alone makes him the dominant force.|
runners_data.comment: Sandy Craic was runner-up last time and has been placed in four of her last six starts, fresh again just 12 days later with solid form over today's distance. The yard's cold trainer form is a mild concern, but she looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: Arrives with a string of poor efforts on soft and standard ground, a headgear flag, and a worrying tendency to fade in the finish; even on good ground, his form reads as a horse who is out of his depth, and he represents the biggest liability in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Scheffler wears cheekpieces and has form over today's distance, with a third the pick of his last four starts. He remains without a win in that spell, and last time's below-par run is the concern.

runners_data.name: Leelawadee
runners_data.note: Michael Dods is in strong form at 4/28 over 14 days, and this filly has placed on good ground before; however, she is a genuine hold-up type running in a field where the rear positions are already taken — her race will be run from further forward than ideal, and the 3lb claimer Rhys Elliott has limited options tactically.|
runners_data.comment: Leelawadee is winless in a run of three starts, though her finishing positions have edged forward each time, and she rates as the outsider here. Distance form is her one obvious asset heading into this.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's horse has won and placed multiple times over a mile on good ground and is back in trip from a below-par nine-furlong effort; his prominent style allows him to track Sandy Craic throughout, and last-time-out winner status over C&D gives him genuine place claims at minimum.|
runners_data.comment: Hatamoto won last time out and returns quickly, just 13 days later, already holding form over today's distance in cheekpieces. Barring that latest success his form has been up and down, so consistency remains the query.

races.paceDynamic: Sandy Craic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no other natural leader to challenge, should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates and control the tempo throughout the mile. Hatamoto is the only other prominent-type and will likely settle just behind Sandy Craic in second, meaning the pace is set by one horse with minimal pressure — a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a searching test. Lady Britain and Leelawadee are the hold-up types, though Leelawadee has been redistributed to midfield on the map as the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than can all race from the rear in a five-runner heat; Lady Britain is the more natural closer and the likelier of the two to secure a rearward pitch. This race shape — a lone leader dictating an honest but unhurried pace — favours prominent racers who can track the front-runner and pounce, giving Hatamoto a natural positional advantage, though Lady Britain's proven closer profile over this trip on good ground means she could arrive late if the pace proves too steady.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sandy Craic Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic leads unopposed and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that denies closers enough run.
scenarios.body: Sandy Craic dictates from the front at a pace that suits himself, never coming off the bridle until pressed in the final furlong, and Hatamoto tracks throughout to inherit the runner-up spot at minimum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic's pace is just fast enough to stop the closers but Hatamoto tracks perfectly and runs past late.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto sits a length off Sandy Craic's heels throughout and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong, picking off the leader who has given all; Sandy Craic holds on for a place.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic sets a genuinely strong early gallop that blows up the prominent runners and leaves a true late run available.
scenarios.body: Lady Britain, held up off a fast pace, threads through a tiring field in the closing stages and finishes powerfully; her two wins over this trip on good ground suggest she is the most capable closer in the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Mess Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and a bunched finish produces an unexpected winner.
scenarios.body: With only five runners, a slow early pace could see the field bunch entering the final two furlongs and reduce the race to a sprint, giving Leelawadee — a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield — any chance she has; form concerns make this the most speculative outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sandy Craic's early sections — if Conor Whiteley allows him to roll along at a comfortable clip unchallenged, the race is effectively over before the straight and he becomes very hard to peg back.

Watch Lady Britain's position from the gates — a 308-day layoff means she may need the race to develop slowly to land her finishing effort, and if she is too far back early she risks being left with too much to do over just a mile.

Watch Hatamoto's jumping off — if he misses the break and cannot get his natural position tracking the leader, his chance is materially diminished as there is no cover or pace to chase into in a five-runner field.

Watch Scheffler's behaviour in the early stages given the headgear flag; if he contests the pace or travels poorly, he could inject a brief mid-race complication that temporarily disrupts Sandy Craic's rhythm.

Watch Leelawadee's opening furlong — if Rhys Elliott cannot find a natural position with a true hold-up type in a small field, she will either have to race greener than ideal or sit last and cover too much ground late.

races.name: Sell Your Business With Anderson Barrowcliff Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Won on Soft at five furlongs but has four recent finishes of 4th or worse; a true hold-up horse whose Good-ground record reads 3/9 with no wins, so going and race shape both conspire against her here, placed in mid-division only because there are too many rear-runners in this field.
runners_data.comment: Yellow Diamonds has finished fourth in three of her last five starts, a picture of consistency, and already holds form over today's distance. She has one win in that spell and, on that steady profile, she gets the vote as our selection.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this hold-up three-year-old back out 21 days after last run; Good-ground form of 8/11 with one win and two places gives little confidence, and being forced closer to the pace than he naturally prefers compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Under The Radar has yet to find a placing in his last five starts, each finish outside the frame. He does have experience over today's distance and is fairly fresh, but such form gives little cause for optimism here.

runners_data.name: Davorge Nation
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's runner won over 5f on Good ground earlier in the season, which is the chief form angle; he's a natural off-the-pace horse, but the map places him in mid-division because the field is overloaded with hold-up types, so he'll need gaps to open late.
runners_data.comment: Davorge Nation rates last of this nine but won four starts back, following up with a third next time, showing some ability on his day. His last two efforts have been well below that level, and a lengthy gap since adds to the doubts.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Sean Kirrane partners a horse with the best Good-ground profile in the race (2W4P from 9 runs), and his proximity style suits the anticipated one-paced lead perfectly; the paddock headgear note suggests connections are confident of a forward show.
runners_data.comment: Simba's Pride won twice earlier in this six-race sequence and the finishing positions have been improving again after a mid-table dip, down to third last time out. He returns quickly in cheekpieces with form over today's distance already, a fair profile in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Houndhill
runners_data.note: Alex Jary (3lb claim) takes the ride for Nigel Tinkler on a three-year-old who won over 5f at Sandown last time, returning here just 15 days later; Good-ground form is sparse (0W1P from 5 runs), but fresh legs and recency are the main angles.
runners_data.comment: Houndhill won three starts back but both subsequent runs have ended unplaced, a clear dip in form after that success. He does have form over today's distance and returns quickly, though the recent placings make him hard to trust fully here.

runners_data.name: Vinciamo
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner has three places from six starts on Good ground and wears a hood, suggesting he can switch off and produce a late effort; however, he is a genuine hold-up horse that this pace shape pushes forward of his comfort zone, so the style mismatch tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Vinciamo is winless in his last five starts but was runner-up last time out and again three starts back, races in a tongue-tie, and already holds form over today's distance. A well-below-par ninth in between shows the inconsistency that leaves him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Straight Ahead
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster has drawn a blank in the last 10 with this yard's runners (T14:0/10), and Straight Ahead's Good-ground form reads 0W2P; he won twice on Standard and will need either a pace collapse or a clear switch to the stands rail to threaten from his true hold-up role.
runners_data.comment: Straight Ahead won twice in the middle of this sequence and holds solid form over today's distance, but his latest run was well below that level. Bouncing back from a below-par eighth last time is the obvious question after such a promising two-race spell.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's consistent five-furlong specialist has 1W2P from 13 Good-ground starts, a record that suggests placing rather than winning; James Sullivan takes the ride but the horse's natural off-pace style makes it hard for him to benefit from a lone-leader scenario.
runners_data.comment: Angel Numbers has twice finished runner-up in her last six starts and already holds form over today's distance, returning inside three weeks of that finishing sequence. She remains without a win in that spell, and last time's fourth was short of her best efforts.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's mare is the only genuine front-runner in the race; her STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she usually races more prominently than outright lead, but here she inherits the role by default and could prove hard to pass if she settles well through the first two furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Empress Olivia won four starts back, the standout of her recent form, and she already holds form over today's distance. Her last two efforts were both below that level, leaving fitness the main doubt.

races.paceDynamic: Empress Olivia is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this nine-runner five-furlong heat, she is set to bowl along uncontested from the gates and dictate a sustainable, rhythm-based gallop. Simba's Pride is the only other horse mapped prominently, giving Empress Olivia a clear buffer before the chasing pack; the remaining seven runners — including Vinciamo, Yellow Diamonds, Under The Radar and Davorge Nation — are true hold-up types whose natural position is off the pace, though the field contains so many of them that several will inevitably be shuffled wider into mid-division rather than sitting where they prefer. On Good ground over five furlongs at Thirsk, a lone leader setting a measured pace tends to be a durable advantage, and the race shape strongly favours horses that can track the lead through the first two furlongs and pounce in the final hundred yards — Simba's Pride, with clean proximity to the pace, is the archetype, while genuine closers will need a strong sectional collapse at the front that a lone, unhurried Empress Olivia is unlikely to provide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Empress Olivia Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia breaks cleanly and Simba's Pride tracks without applying early pressure, she controls a sustainable gallop and holds on.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on Good ground over five furlongs at Thirsk can dictate tempo and conserve energy through the bend, giving her every chance of lasting home; Simba's Pride, the closest pursuer with consistent Good-ground form (2W4P on Good), is best placed to reel her in but may find the gap too small.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia sets a slightly brisk early pace and Simba's Pride sits neatly behind before launching a decisive run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Simba's Pride's strong proximity profile and the fact that all nine of his runs on Good ground have seen him placed or better makes him the standout beneficiary if Empress Olivia gives him a target to peg back; a runner-up finish at the minimum becomes a winning one here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Materialises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply in the final furlong and genuine hold-up types get a clear passage on the outside.
scenarios.body: Vinciamo has three placings from six Good-ground starts and has the tactical speed to finish powerfully if the front end fades; Angel Numbers and Straight Ahead could also grab a slice of the prize, though all three are partially racing out of their natural position in this pace shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Defies Pattern
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually strong, the field fans wide, and a runner with fresh legs capitalises on an unusually open home straight.
scenarios.body: Houndhill landed a win last time at Sandown on Standard ground and returns on a short turnaround, giving her a fitness edge if others are flattered by the map; Davorge Nation, who won on Good ground at five furlongs, is the other live outsider if gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: Empress Olivia's break from the stalls is pivotal — if she misses the kick, there is no other natural leader to fill the vacuum and the race shape becomes scrambled.

Simba's Pride is the horse most likely to profit if the pace is genuine; watch whether Sean Kirrane takes a position directly behind the leader or drifts wide, as a clear run from two furlongs out is his key tactical requirement.

With four confirmed hold-up types redistributed into mid-division, watch the early stages for crowding on the rail — a bump or wide draw could cost Vinciamo or Angel Numbers crucial ground on the short five-furlong trip.

Houndhill won last time out but returns on just 15 days' rest with a 3lb claimer; if the horse shows any signs of post-race fatigue in the paddock or is slowly away, the recency edge disappears quickly.

Trainer Craig Lidster has registered zero winners from his last 10 runners (T14:0/10) — Straight Ahead would need to significantly outrun the stable's current form cycle to factor, which is worth noting when assessing odds.

races.name: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over 7f at Yarmouth on good ground 12 days ago; Dylan Cunha's yard is winless in 17 over the past fortnight which is a concern, and the step up to a mile on a track where this horse has no sim-going wins is another flag — the style fit rating reflects it racing slightly out of comfort zone in what is mapped as a prominent role.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back shows he retains ability, but three well-beaten efforts have followed and last time's sixth was no better. He has raced over today's trip before and wears a tongue-tie, with a place in this company the realistic target now.

runners_data.name: Bridgefoot Rambler
runners_data.note: Hanlon-trained four-year-old who ran over this trip at Catterick 38 days ago finishing ninth; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear but the volume of closers in this field means it is unlikely to find that berth uncontested, and its 0W0P record on similar going saps confidence.
runners_data.comment: Nothing better than two sixths in her last four starts, and the bottom-rated runner in the field on our figures, she has plenty to find. A 38-day break and blinkers again do not obviously help her cause, though she has raced over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has hit the frame at 8f on good ground, recording a placed effort at this trip recently; races from the back naturally and is best served by a strong pace scenario — the sim-going record of 8 from 11 is notably poor and limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures on the back of a clear second among her last five starts, and she has raced over today's trip before. Yet to win in that sequence and returning from a 30-day break, but clearly feared on pure form.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran who has been highly consistent at this trip and going combination, finishing in the first four in multiple recent outings including two seconds on good ground; Ruth Carr's yard has had two winners from 20 in the last fortnight and this horse's genuine hold-up style makes it one of the truest closers in the race.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts among his last five starts underline solid ability, and he has raced over today's trip before while continuing in cheekpieces. Yet to win in that sequence, but rated third in this field and clearly held in respect.

runners_data.name: Create
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon sends this six-year-old here 32 days after its last run; the form string of -80004 is uninspiring but it has placed once on similar going from 15 runs — though it is a natural hold-up type, the crowded rear means it is likely to race closer to the pace than suits, dampening its prospects.
runners_data.comment: A fourth stands out from an otherwise modest run of five starts, and a 32-day break plus continued use of cheekpieces do little to inspire confidence. She has raced over today's trip before, but yet to win in that sequence and rated only mid-table here.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Nigel Tinkler whose yard has been among the more active in recent weeks with three winners from 23; prominent-style racer with a win at this distance and going combination who could find himself tracking Aspire To Glory closely — the 21-day absence and consistent form string of 536763 suggests fitness but not dominance.
runners_data.comment: Two thirds among her last six starts show she goes well enough at this level, and she has raced over today's trip before with a 21-day gap no concern. Yet to win in that sequence, more a frame chance than a leading fancy.

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old who won over this exact trip on good ground at this course in his penultimate start (1/8f/GOO in hist); Michael Dods has four winners from 28 over the past fortnight and this horse's authentic hold-up style is backed by proven course form — the tongue-tie is retained and 11 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: A fourth last time out just 11 days ago, having won two starts back, means Langholm arrives in good heart. He has raced over today's trip before wearing cheekpieces and a tongue-tie, with the odd blank effort the only blot.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's seven-year-old last ran just eight days ago and brings strong recent good-ground form including four placings from five runs on good; a proven hold-up operator but with the rear of the field congested it is likely to be pushed into a midfield spot it has not historically used — the style displacement is the primary tactical risk here.
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back is the highlight of a mixed sequence of six runs, and she returns quickly after a rapid 8-day turnaround. She has raced over today's trip before in cheekpieces, but yet to win in that sequence and looks a fringe contender at best.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old carries a ⚠ fade flag and has not won or placed on similar going in four attempts; operating at a lighter weight of 127lbs as a three-year-old, but the tendency to weaken in the finish — combined with being a natural closer displaced into midfield — makes it hard to frame as a winning candidate.
runners_data.comment: Nothing better than a sixth from four recent starts, and rated near the bottom of this field on our figures, he has plenty to prove. A 31-day break does not help his cause, though he has raced over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Park Lane Penny
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old placed over this trip at Thirsk in its penultimate start (2/8f/GOO), which is directly relevant course and distance form; Tom Eaves takes the ride and this is a hold-up type whose recent course placing is a genuine positive — the 11-day turnaround is no issue.
runners_data.comment: A second stands out from an otherwise modest run of four starts, but she's yet to win in that sequence and the yard is misfiring — just 1 winner from 27 runners lately. Has raced over today's trip before and returns quickly, which counts in her favour.

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's three-year-old has been placed on soft but has a poor record on good ground (2 from 8 in similar going), and while it races with a tongue-tie as a natural hold-up horse, the 26-day absence and modest sim-going profile make it difficult to recommend beyond each-way interest in the right shape.
runners_data.comment: A third three starts back is the highlight of an otherwise ordinary sequence of five runs, and she continues in cheekpieces and a tongue-tie having raced over today's trip before. Yet to win in that sequence, she looks capable of no more than a minor role.

runners_data.name: Regal Knight
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's three-year-old has placed on good ground over this trip recently (3/8f/GOO and 4/8f/GOO in hist) and Silvestre De Sousa is a top-class booking; a genuine hold-up type by nature but it is likely to race in midfield rather than from the rear, and the consistent placed form suggests it could be dangerous if the race develops a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without excelling, with a third and two fourths among his last five starts, he has raced over today's trip before and continues in cheekpieces. Yet to win in that sequence and rated only 44 by us, he looks the type to fill a place at best.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's three-year-old won over this trip on good ground 28 days ago (1/8f/GOO) and brings the most relevant and recent winning form in the race at this distance and going; Joanna Mason rides and the visor is retained — a prominent type who travelled well to score last time and could again slot in just off the pace-setter.
runners_data.comment: She won last time out, backing that up with two thirds and a second earlier in this sequence of six starts, and she has raced over today's trip before. A 28-day break is the only query, but on pure form she rates a major threat to all.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival willing to press from the front — I Can Boogy and Trucial Pearl have prominent tendencies but neither is a natural leader, meaning Aspire To Glory can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo over the mile. With a sustainable gallop set from the front, the race is likely to develop as a conventional test of stamina and finishing quality rather than a dash from a searching pace, favouring those who can travel comfortably in mid-division and produce a clean late challenge. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear — Bridgefoot Rambler, Create, Without Delay, Here Comes Louie, Queenies Pal and Regal Knight are all genuine closers but have been redistributed to midfield because there is simply no room for all of them to race from their natural position; those most likely to actually secure a rear position include Copper And Five, Can I Kiss You and Langholm, who are the more established hold-up operators. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled pace set by a lone leader favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of Aspire To Glory and produce a progressive turn-of-foot in the closing stages, giving the edge to prominent racers and genuine one-two-three hold-up horses over those redistributed closers who may end up too close to the pace for their own good.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire To Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory bowls along unchallenged and sets a genuine but unhurried tempo that suits those tracking close.
scenarios.body: Aspire To Glory dictates on a tight rein, with I Can Boogy and Trucial Pearl slotting in directly behind; the controlled gallop compresses the field and those racing in the first four gain a decisive positional advantage entering the final two furlongs. Prominent horses and those who can travel handy get first run on the leaders, and true hold-up types who cannot get to the front rank find themselves blocked or finishing too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a gap for closers to close through.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early gallop — perhaps if I Can Boogy or Trucial Pearl pushes forward and tests Aspire To Glory — burns off the front rank in the final furlong, opening a clear late lane for genuine closers tracking from mid-division. Copper And Five and Langholm, both proven hold-up types on good ground at this trip, are best placed among the true rear-division horses to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If I Can Boogy or Trucial Pearl pushes hard to challenge Aspire To Glory before the turn, creating a contested pace duel.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop between the prominent types sets a stronger tempo than Aspire To Glory intended, and the front two exhaust themselves in a battle that leaves the door ajar for a single progressive challenger to sweep past in the final furlong. This shape benefits a horse that has been tracking patiently just off the duel in third or fourth and possesses a clean turn of foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the majority of redistributed hold-up types race out of role in midfield, causing crowding and producing a messy, strung-out finish.
scenarios.body: With Create, Without Delay, Regal Knight and others forced into unfamiliar midfield positions, the mid-race order becomes congested and disorganised, creating interference that disrupts the expected finishing order. In this chaotic shape the least affected runners — those who have genuinely settled into their natural position early — benefit most, with Park Lane Penny's consistency at this trip and Trucial Pearl's recent win on good ground giving them the best chance of threading through.

watchPoints.text: Aspire To Glory is the only confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field — if it gets even a lenient early lead it could prove very hard to reel in from the front, making its run in the early stages the most critical watch-point of the race.

Trucial Pearl won over this exact trip and going 28 days ago and has clear form credentials to match the leader for pace early; watch whether Joanna Mason elects to push forward and test Aspire To Glory's front-running resolve or settle just off the pace.

The majority of hold-up types — including Create, Without Delay, Queenies Pal and Regal Knight — will be racing out of their natural position in a congested midfield; monitor the early stages for crowding or interference that could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Copper And Five and Langholm are the two most convincing genuine closers with proven form at this trip on good ground — if the pace softens and they cannot get cover from the rear, their entire race strategy is compromised.

Regal Knight holds the most consistent recent placed form in the field at this trip and going combination and carries a top jockey booking in Silvestre De Sousa — a horse to keep onside if the pace develops strongly enough to reward a hold-up run.

races.name: Meijer Celebration Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher with a place at 6f on Good going last time; Zak Wheatley keeps the ride and the drop back from 8f to 7f is the right move, suits a sprint-finish scenario where his late thrust counts.|
runners_data.comment: In the frame twice in his last five outings, including a close third last time, and has raced over today's trip before; a 31-day break is the only query. Yet to win in that sequence, but our rating makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's mare has strong 7f Good form with two placed efforts at this trip last month; James Sullivan knows her well and the sim-going record (10/15) gives genuine confidence in conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up finishes among his last six starts show he retains solid form, and he has raced over today's trip before, with a 24-day break no concern. Yet to win in that sequence, but the sort capable of running into the frame again.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran who is actually a true hold-up runner by nature but placed here in midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; Tristan Davidson sends him out fresh on 8 days rest and his 7f Good record is solid with a win included.|
runners_data.comment: Third twice in her last six starts and quick to reappear just eight days on, having raced over today's trip before. Yet to win in that sequence, but fit enough now to feature again among the leading contenders.

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.note: Very limited recent form — just three runs and no wins or places — and though Cam Hardie is capable, the horse's natural finishing style is compromised because this field offers no real pace to chase; bottom-weight counts in its favour.|
runners_data.comment: Two fifths and a sixth from just three recent starts, a lightly raced sort who has raced over today's trip before, drawn stall 10. Yet to win in that sequence and rated only 47 by us, she has plenty to find to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has finished no closer than fourth in five starts, with all runs at 6-7f on Good or Standard; Joanna Mason takes the mount but the form string (7/8644) offers little encouragement and the horse's genuine rear-of-field style is squeezed here.|
runners_data.comment: A pair of fourths headline a modest run of five starts, and he has raced over today's trip before. Yet to win in that sequence, he looks capable of another midfield finish rather than a big step forward.

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win on Standard at 6f and a recent second at the same trip; Kevin & Lauren Frost's runner has been racing off the pace consistently and the step up to 7f on Good turf is an interesting unknown — watching to see if William Pyle rides more prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Elashgar won four starts back and has raced over today's trip before; a below-par sixth last time is the only real blot, but he remains a leading danger on our figures.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Has headgear (p) fitted and boasts three placed efforts from eight runs on Good going — Philip Kirby's mare is a genuine stayer at heart (best form at 7-8f), and with Clifford Lee aboard she could be quietly suited if the race lacks real early pace.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of her last five starts, including a second two starts back, she has raced over today's trip before and continues in cheekpieces. Yet to win in that sequence, but capable of another respectable showing on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Forever Twenty
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old has headgear (t) and has placed twice including a third at 8f on Good; Alex Jary claims 3lb which helps at the weights, and the horse's true late style may be best expressed if it can drift forward naturally in the absence of genuine front-runners.|
runners_data.comment: Two thirds in her last six starts hint at some ability, but she's yet to win in that sequence, and the yard is misfiring badly - just 1 winner from 27 runners in the last fortnight. She has raced over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Crown Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Limited three-run form (best a fourth) and all runs have come at 7-8f on Good or Standard; Silvestre De Sousa is a major jockey booking for OR=52 company and that upgrade in rider quality is the primary reason to take note here.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced with just three recent starts and nothing better than a fourth to show, she also returns from a 32-day break for a yard managing only 1 winner from 27 runners lately. Has raced over today's trip before, but sits bottom of these figures.

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's three-year-old has shown headgear (t) and a consistent record of finishing mid-to-rear (no wins, no places) across seven runs on Good or Soft; Rhys Elliott claims 5lb but the form (868-87) makes this a benchmark runner rather than a winning contender.|
runners_data.comment: A run of five finishes no better than sixth tells its own story, and a 38-day absence does nothing to ease the doubts. He has raced over today's trip before and continues in a tongue-tie, but little here suggests a much-improved showing.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this field carrying a hold-up style rating, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse willing to dominate from the front — meaning the early gallop at Thirsk over seven furlongs is likely to be cautious, dawdling, and highly tactical. The field will bunch together in the early stages, with runners jostling for position before a collective sprint develops from the home turn, turning this into a dash for the line rather than a true test of stamina. Emerald Army, Captain Cess, and Elashgar are the best-credentialled finishers based on recent form, and in a sprint finish the premium falls on those who can produce a sharp, sustained late burst from a decent position. This race shape heavily favours hold-up runners with strong finishing speed and a proven record on Good turf — a late-rush profile is the dominant archetype here, provided the jockey times the run to perfection. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can physically accommodate at the rear; horses like Coconut Bay, Forever Twenty, Crown Of Dreams, Misemerald, and Breeze Star are mapped to midfield but are true late-runners by nature, with those carrying the best recent form — particularly Coconut Bay and Forever Twenty — most likely to secure a forward enough pitch if the pace is genuinely slow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and the field bunches before a furious dash from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The absence of any pace-setter means horses will travel in a tight group before a mass cavalry charge develops inside the final two furlongs, rewarding those with the sharpest finishing kick on Good turf.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate but not genuinely slow gallop allows the redistributed midfield horses to travel prominently and grind opponents down.
scenarios.body: Horses mapped to midfield — particularly Coconut Bay and Misemerald — get a better pitch than their natural style suggests, allowing them to time their run from a more advantageous position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jockey Outwits The Crowd
scenarios.trigger: If a canny jockey pushes their mount forward early to steal a march and sets a solo uncontested lead by default.
scenarios.body: With no horse naturally bred to lead, a bold ride from any jockey in the field could result in an accidental front-runner who dictates at a sedate pace and proves very hard to catch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Crowding
scenarios.trigger: If the field masses in the final furlong and wide-running traffic causes interference that compromises several closers.
scenarios.body: The sheer density of hold-up horses converging simultaneously creates the risk that some are impeded or switched wide too late, allowing a horse racing cleanly near the outside to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Crown Of Dreams is ridden by Silvestre De Sousa — a significant jockey upgrade on OR=52 rated form — watch whether De Sousa pushes forward early to manufacture a position that delivers an uncontested lead by default in a field with no natural pace-setter.

Coconut Bay arrives on just 8 days' rest and is the only horse in the field with a win at this trip on Good going in his recent history — if Jason Hart reads the slow early pace and positions him in the first three, he becomes a serious danger.

Forever Twenty and Crown Of Dreams share the same trainer Ivan Furtado — with two runners in a small ten-horse field, watch for any stable booking signals or market moves that indicate which is the preferred runner.

The entire field is classified as hold-up style, creating a very real risk of a false pace — if no horse commits to the front in the first two furlongs at Thirsk, the field could crawl to halfway before a furious sprint develops, compressing the form and making draw and position in the final furlong critical.

Emerald Army's sim-going record of 10/15 is the strongest in the field on Good turf at this trip, making James Sullivan's positioning in the final quarter-mile the key tactical watch point of the race.

races.name: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: Consistent if frustrating hold-up performer for O'Meara with strong sim-going record (11/15 on Good) and solid recent run 12 days ago; needs a stronger pace than Military Leader is likely to generate over this mile, which is the central concern.|
runners_data.comment: Capital Guarantee is fresh, back only 12 days after his latest run, and already holds form over today's distance. He remains without a win in his last six starts, and the yard is out of form, but he brings the highest official rating into this field.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: William Pyle takes the ride on this Barron-trained hold-up type who has placed four times from his last five on Good ground — best of the deep closers in terms of consistency, but similarly dependent on a proper gallop being set that this race shape may not provide.|
runners_data.comment: Degale shares the fastest figures on the clock of these six and already holds form over today's distance, back just 12 days after his latest run. He remains without a win in his last six starts, with modest finishing positions the obvious blot on that record.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old carries headgear (visor) and has placed five times from 15 on this ground for Joanna Mason — as the second prominent-style runner she is best placed to track Military Leader and, if she can match his early fractions, she becomes the most natural challenger from the front group.|
runners_data.comment: Harswell Ruby was runner-up last time out and returns quickly again nine days later, sharing the fastest figures on the clock here in cheekpieces. She remains without a win in her last six starts, with mostly mid-field finishes before that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes over on this Phillip Makin-trained front-runner who has won twice this season and possesses a STYLE_FIT flag indicating he is sometimes placed differently — but here as the lone confirmed leader he is fully in his element, and his Good-ground sim-going record (4/14) is the primary caution against assuming dominance is automatic.|
runners_data.comment: Military Leader has been well placed, with two wins and two runner-up efforts in his last five starts, and holds form over today's distance in blinkers. He is only rated on a par with his official mark, and the lengthy break since his latest run is the concern.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: O'Meara's eight-year-old is a natural front-runner or prominent racer by inclination but, with Military Leader in the field, he is unlikely to secure that position and instead finds himself pushed back into unfamiliar territory — his recent form (0-9576) has been modest and racing out of role further dims his prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Cosmos Raj has failed to find a placing in his last five starts and the yard is currently out of form, leaving him rated last of these six. He does have experience over today's distance, though, and quicker figures on the clock than his placings suggest.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Easterby's seven-year-old is genuinely a hold-up specialist with an excellent recent placed record (three seconds, two thirds from his last five on Good), but he is shown in midfield because the race holds more rear-of-field types than can all sit there — his true position will be further back, and without a strong pace to aim at the scenario that suits him is the least likely to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Barley has been rock-solid, placed in four of his last six starts including third last time out, and is fresh again 12 days later with form over today's distance in cheekpieces. He remains without a win in that spell, but the consistency makes him hard to leave out.

races.paceDynamic: Military Leader is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to dispute the lead aggressively, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this mile at Thirsk. Harswell Ruby is the only other prominent-style horse with a credible claim to tracking position just off the pace, giving the leaders a small group while the remainder settle in behind. The field actually contains more pace-inclined runners than the map can accommodate — Cosmos Raj is a natural prominent racer and Barley a true hold-up type, but both are displaced in the shape, meaning neither is likely to race where they are most comfortable. This setup — a single uncontested front-runner setting a measured, even tempo — classically favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can track within range and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Military Leader dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the field settles into a single-file rhythm behind him.
scenarios.body: Military Leader sets the terms and a sustainable pace means those tracking closest — Harswell Ruby and any horse who gets cover in the slipstream — are best placed to mount a challenge in the final two furlongs. The hold-up horses face the classic problem of too little pace to exploit, and the prominent trackers who stay close to the leader are rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Military Leader's gallop is genuinely strong enough for the deeper runners to close from well off the pace in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Capital Guarantee or Degale, both genuine hold-up types with decent sim-going form on Good, would need to produce an unusually strong late run — only viable if the early pace proves faster than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Wins Easily
scenarios.trigger: If Military Leader's controlled tempo is so slow that the field can never land a blow and he simply strolls home unchallenged.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to put Military Leader under early pressure, he could conserve enough energy to quicken clear at the two-furlong pole before rivals can respond. His Good-ground form is limited (4/14 sim-going) but at this level an uncontested lead compensates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Chaos Breaks
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmos Raj or another displaced prominent type refuses to settle and forces a faster-than-expected early tempo, scrambling the race shape.
scenarios.body: A strung-out, pressured gallop would open the door for hold-up horses to finish powerfully but, given Barley and Cosmos Raj are not operating in their natural roles, the execution of that scenario is unreliable. Any disorder in the pace would most likely benefit whoever tracks Military Leader most closely rather than the genuine back-markers.

watchPoints.text: Military Leader's ability to control the pace without being pressured is the single biggest factor — if PJ McDonald bowls along at a fair clip unchallenged for the first five furlongs, the prominent tracker Harswell Ruby becomes the immediate danger.|

Cosmos Raj's tendency to race prominently could lead to an unintended duel for position in the early stages if he refuses to drop back — monitor whether Mark Winn settles him quickly or if he pushes forward and disrupts Military Leader's rhythm.|

Barley's form figures (3-2-3-2-6 on Good) show he handles this surface well but Sean Kirrane will need luck in running from the rear if the pace is pedestrian — watch for whether he can find a clear passage turning for home.|

Capital Guarantee has a poor recent form string (020906) despite his sim-going record; Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) is a factor and the low weight helps, but he has been beaten a long way out of the frame in his last two runs and needs something to change.|

Going is listed as unknown across all six runners — if the track rides faster or firmer than anticipated, front-runner Military Leader's stamina reserves over a mile become more important, and his softer-ground wins in 2025 are a mild flag worth tracking at the off.|
